headline: Regional Lodging and Dixie National Forest Access
reservation: Staying in Tropic or Panguitch requires separate bookings from National Park campgrounds. While Dixie National Forest trails are generally open, specific recreation sites may require local day-use fees or seasonal permits; verify current status with the Forest Service.

days.title: Red Rocks and Gateway Orientation

stops.name: Red Canyon Visitor Center
stops.detail: Explore the crimson limestone formations along Scenic Byway 12 before entering the National Park.

stops.name: Arches Trail
stops.detail: A short, steep hike in Red Canyon providing views of multiple natural windows without the park crowds.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transfers between Panguitch and Red Canyon.
days.note: Red Canyon offers a similar aesthetic to Bryce but is managed by the Forest Service.

days.title: The Great Amphitheater Loop

stops.name: Inspiration Point
stops.detail: Observe the three levels of the amphitheater and the density of the hoodoo 'forest'.

stops.name: Mossy Cave Trail
stops.detail: Visit this low-elevation trail near Tropic to see a dripping alcove and a waterfall created by a pioneer ditch.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; traffic can be slow near the park's entrance station.
days.note: Mossy Cave has a separate parking area outside the main park fee station.

days.title: High Plateau Discovery
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Bryce Canyon City

stops.name: Fairyland Point
stops.detail: A quieter overlook located at the very beginning of the park road offering a distinct perspective.

stops.name: Paria View
stops.detail: Face the hoodoos that catch the afternoon light, looking toward the Paria River Valley.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for exploring various viewpoints along the northern plateau.
days.note: Fairyland Point is sometimes bypassed by the shuttle; check current routes.

intel.title: Mossy Cave Constraints
intel.text: The parking area for Mossy Cave is small and frequently full between 10 AM and 4 PM. Plan to visit very early or late in the day to avoid parking on the shoulder of Highway 12.

intel.title: Regional Dead Zones
intel.text: Connectivity drops significantly as you head east from Tropic toward Cannonville. Paper maps are recommended for exploring the backroads of the Dixie National Forest.

intel.title: Scenic Byway 12 Logistics
intel.text: Fuel is available in Tropic and Bryce Canyon City, but prices and availability vary. Ensure your tank is full before heading toward the more remote Escalante region.

intel.title: Afternoon Storms
intel.text: Summer monsoons can bring sudden lightning to the exposed rims by 2 PM. Retreat to lower elevations or your vehicle if you hear thunder.

intel.title: Winter Road Closures
intel.text: High-elevation roads in the region can close during and after snowstorms. Check the Utah Department of Transportation (UDOT) for real-time alerts.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at CDC airport, proceed through Cedar Breaks (if open) to Panguitch for supplies, and continue to your regional base.
plan.vehicle: A high-clearance vehicle is recommended if you plan to explore forest roads outside the main paved scenic byways.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset Point lives up to its name for late-day photography; verify local sunset times at the Visitor Center.
